name: Delta Lake
model: Open table format: SQL tables as Parquet files plus an ordered JSON transaction log (_delta_log), mainly used from Spark and Databricks
engine_note: Not a server: Parquet files in object storage; each commit adds the next numbered log file, which is the table's metadata pointer
consistency: Per-table ACID by optimistic concurrency: read snapshot, write files, validate and commit the next log entry; conflicting writers retry or fail. Readers keep a consistent snapshot. WriteSerializable default, Serializable option.
scaling: Storage scales with object storage; compute is Spark, Databricks, Trino, DuckDB or delta-rs, scaled separately.
version_note: Delta Lake for Spark release; 3.3.3 maintenance release 2026-08-12 for the older line.
reach: Reach for it when you already run Spark or Databricks and want ACID tables, time travel and upserts on files in your own object storage.
avoid: Avoid for small data or app-path writes; outside Spark/Databricks, check your engine's Delta support first or prefer Iceberg.
escape: data too large for one database, kept as open files in object storage with ACID commits
chat: Long-term archive of messages and usage events in object storage, for training data and analytics.
notes: Table format, not a server. Isolation levels from Databricks docs; delta.io concurrency page confirms optimistic three-stage commit and snapshot reads. Concurrent writers on S3 historically needed a log store with put-if-absent (DynamoDB); not re-confirmed on the fetched page, so left out of the cell. Microsoft Fabric OneLake using Delta not re-fetched today; unconfirmed. The Tabular acquisition (2024-06-04) brought Iceberg's creators to Databricks, which develops Delta; see iceberg.json.
